Phil Mickelson. Lefty. An American professional golfer who won 6 major championships as one of Tiger Woods's primary rivals from the 2000s through the 2020s. Known for his creative shot-making, aggressive style, and longevity competing across three decades, he became one of golf's most beloved and entertaining figures.

He won 6 major championships: 3 Masters in 2004, 2006, and 2010, 2 PGA Championships in 2005 and 2021, and 1 Open Championship in 2013. In 2021, he won the PGA Championship at age 50, becoming the oldest winner of a major championship in professional golf history. Mickelson was famous for his creativity and willingness to attempt flop shots and unconventional techniques that distinguished him from peers.

He competed primarily on the PGA Tour from 1992 through 2022, demonstrating extraordinary professional longevity. He won 45 PGA Tour events and numerous international tournaments, establishing himself as one of the most prolific winners in modern golf. He engaged in one of golf's most famous rivalries with Tiger Woods throughout the 2000s and 2010s. He was known for his accessibility to fans, humor, and competitive fire that made him one of the most popular golfers of his era.

Mickelson's career spanned generations. Tiger Woods was his primary rival throughout his peak years. Rory McIlroy was a contemporary competitor during the modern era. Tom Watson was a predecessor who inspired Mickelson's commitment to longevity.
